records.title: When Too Many Cooks Spoil the Broth: Three Failure Modes of Multi-Agent LLM Reliability

publication_status.basis: Fresh Crossref publisher-deposited metadata; publisher full text unavailable to this check.

observed_evidence.finding: Title, author list, DOI, venue and date match the saved source. Author ORCID also lists this work.

The abstract already reports self-confidence/peer-resistance dissociation, verifier-dependent propagation differences, and correlated failure across model families. These broad observations cannot be claimed as new in C1.
ACM landing page could not be read by web tool; official PDF request returned HTTP 403. No paywall or access control was bypassed.
DOI/title/author searches did not locate a matching legal author manuscript or arXiv full text in this check. This is not evidence that none exists.

unresolved_questions: Does the full paper already compare out-of-sample predictive validity of peer-resistance and self-confidence at matched calibration?
What are the exact confidence elicitation prompts, wrong-peer generation protocol, datasets, per-item paired results, and uncertainty estimates?
Can an authorized publisher or author-hosted copy and supplementary materials be obtained?

candidate_difference_assessment.decision: Keep novelty gate closed. Feasibility-only pilot may proceed if explicitly separated from novelty approval; do not promote the proposed predictive comparison as a new contribution.

records.title: Contextual Trust Evaluation for Robust Coordination in Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems

publication_status.basis: Official Preprints.org landing page and PDF cover; this check does not establish a later journal publication.

observed_evidence.location: Official landing page and PDF cover
observed_evidence.finding: Title and DOI match. The platform explicitly identifies this version as not peer reviewed.
Trust combines historical performance, interaction quality and consistency; trust informs dynamic role assignment. This is already the central mechanism proposed in C2.

observed_evidence.location: Section IV.B and V, printed pages 7–8
observed_evidence.finding: Evaluation describes success, runtime, communication and trust trajectories; static assignment is an explicit comparator. No dedicated peer-resistance versus self-confidence prediction experiment was found in the inspected full text.
No explicit operational cascade-onset comparison was found in these sections. This limited observation does not establish a meaningful or novel contribution for C2.
Official HTML and 11-page PDF text were readable through web. Direct PDF download returned HTTP 403; web screenshots also failed. No PDF was stored or claimed downloaded.

unresolved_questions: Where are the actual scenario inputs, prompts, code, per-trial results, and uncertainty estimates needed for independent reproduction?
Are there later versions or broader prior works that already test the proposed predictor or cascade measure?
For C2, what operational metric and distinct mechanism would remain after accounting for this existing dynamic assignment baseline?

candidate_difference_assessment.C1: This paper addresses a different trust-coordination setting and does not resolve the missing closest-work full-text comparison.
candidate_difference_assessment.C2: Core mechanism overlaps directly; changing the outcome to cascade-onset is insufficient evidence of novelty. Keep replacement recommendation.
